name: Hymenaeus
title: False Teacher in the Early Church
summary: Hymenaeus was a person in the early Christian church who departed from the true faith and spread false teaching. He claimed that the resurrection had already taken place, thereby undermining the faith of some Christians. Paul mentions him specifically as a warning and an example of apostasy.

keyEvents.title: Delivered to Satan
keyEvents.description: Paul notes that he has delivered Hymenaeus and Alexander to Satan so that they may learn not to blaspheme. This was a form of church discipline for their false teaching and blasphemy.

keyEvents.title: False Teaching about the Resurrection
keyEvents.description: Hymenaeus and Philetus taught that the resurrection had already occurred, which undermined the Christian belief in the future bodily resurrection and destroyed the faith of some.

keyEvents.title: Warning against Empty Talk
keyEvents.description: Paul warns Timothy against the kind of empty and ungodly talk that Hymenaeus represented, because such speech spreads like gangrene in the church.
